record.original_question: A normalized basic sequence (x_n) in a Banach space is called a Rosenthal basis if every normalized block sequence (v_n) of (x_n) has a subsequence equivalent to (x_n). Must every Rosenthal basis be equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space with a normalized basic sequence $(x_n)_{n=1}^\infty$. A normalized block sequence of $(x_n)$ is a sequence $(v_n)$ of unit vectors of the form $v_n = \sum_{i=p_n+1}^{p_{n+1}} a_i x_i$ for some scalars $a_i$ and integers $0 = p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$. Two normalized basic sequences $(y_n)$ and $(z_n)$ are said to be equivalent if there exists a constant $C \geq 1$ such that for every finitely supported sequence of scalars $(a_n)$,
$$C^{-1}\Big\|\sum_n a_n y_n\Big\| \leq \Big\|\sum_n a_n z_n\Big\| \leq C\Big\|\sum_n a_n y_n\Big\|.$$
Call $(x_n)$ a Rosenthal basis if every normalized block sequence $(v_n)$ of $(x_n)$ admits a subsequence which is equivalent to $(x_n)$.

Question: Must every Rosenthal basis be equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of $c_0$ or of $\ell_p$ for some $1 \leq p < \infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: Ferenczi and Pelczar (Bull. London Math. Soc., 2004) proved that under additional uniformity assumptions, a Rosenthal-type basis is equivalent to the unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$. The general problem without such assumptions appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On a question of Haskell P. Rosenthal
status_evidence.snippet: We show that under uniformity or other natural assumptions, a basis with this property is equivalent to the unit vector basis of c_0 or ell_p.
status_evidence.claim: The Rosenthal basis problem is solved only under uniformity or other natural assumptions, suggesting the unconditional version remains open.

status_evidence.title: On a Question of Haskell P. Rosenthal concerning a characterization of c_0 and ell_p
status_evidence.snippet: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society, 2004 — characterization under uniformity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial solution published in 2004 imposing extra assumptions.
